$comment: Art direction per format: identical to winter-morning.json except the photographs. Feed and story use a square GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst image; landscape uses a Sunburst image composed for it (cup in the left third).

copy.label: The winter table
headline: A slow cup
for short days.
copy.body: Black tea with orange peel and clove, steeped for four minutes while the morning light is still low.
copy.cta: Winter Blend No. 3 · In shops from 1 December

situation.exigence: A seasonal blend is released on 1 December. People who already drink tea do not yet know it exists or why it belongs to this time of year.
situation.audience: Tea drinkers scrolling on a phone in the dark hours of early December, mostly before or after work. They pause for a second at most and watch without sound.
constraints: Muted autoplay in a feed: the film must work without sound and from any frame a viewer joins on.
Three formats from one source: 4:5 feed, 9:16 story, 16:9 landscape.
Invented example brand; copy is fixed in the campaign and is not rewritten by the design.
Two generated photographs (GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst), each directed for its formats and approved by the project owner for this demonstration; everything else is code.
situation.kairos: The darkest weeks of the year, the days before the release. The moment the design answers is the low, late winter sunrise that the copy names: the design shows that moment arriving.

criteria.criterion: The film enacts the moment the copy names: it starts in the blue dark of a December morning and ends in low, warm light. The light is the argument for the time of year.
The release date lands last and alone, like the date on a film poster, so the viewer leaves with when.
Made for muted autoplay and a one-second glance: the cup is in the first frame and the headline is read by 1 s, while the light still takes its time. The end state holds long enough to read.
Enargeia: the viewer is placed at the table, not shown a product. The photograph fills the frame, the camera pushes slowly in and the light changes in the room.
The feeling is earned by the scene and not added: no exclamation, no music cue, no effect that is not a property of light, time or film.
The film carries the one practical fact a tea drinker needs: four minutes at 95 °C, shown as time passing.
One reading path: label, headline, body, steeping time, then brand and date. Salience falls in that order.
Craft shows character: a real serif, measured type, legible on the image everywhere, nothing cropped or overflowing in any format.
Nothing is claimed that the brand cannot stand behind: the copy is the campaign's own, and the photograph's origin is recorded in the manifest.
